messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: gmo, rstanarm, and prior specifications
parts:
This discussion hijacked an earlier thread, so I'm moving
it here and adding my own two cents to the end.

> On Feb 28, 2016, at 1:21 AM, Jonah Sol Gabry <jga...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks for sharing the repository. Dustin, is the plan to have users specify their own Stan programs or eventually use a higher level interface like rstanarm? Or both maybe?


> On Feb 28, 2016, at 1:32 AM, Dustin Tran <dustinv...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I think for general models, we’re going to stick to specifying their own Stan programs. For glmer-type models we’ll take some of the internal functions from rstanarm to write the gmo_glmer()/gmo_lmer()/gmo_nlmer() functions, and those 3 functions will closely follow the lme4/rstanarm interfaces.
>
> There’s one exception. For priors on the hyperparameters, I think Andrew wants us to be able to specify a stan program to specify that distribution, rather than to hard-code a set of options.

I think whatever we do it should be consistent across the
interfaces and have them all specify priors in the same way.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: gmo, rstanarm, and prior specifications
parts:
On Sunday, February 28, 2016 at 7:51:54 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> On Feb 28, 2016, at 1:32 AM, Dustin Tran <dustinv...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I think for general models, we’re going to stick to specifying their own Stan programs. For glmer-type models we’ll take some of the internal functions from rstanarm to write the gmo_glmer()/gmo_lmer()/gmo_nlmer() functions, and those 3 functions will closely follow the lme4/rstanarm interfaces.
>
> There’s one exception. For priors on the hyperparameters, I think Andrew wants us to be able to specify a stan program to specify that distribution, rather than to hard-code a set of options.

I think whatever we do it should be consistent across the
interfaces and have them all specify priors in the same way.

For rstanarm, we are not compiling models at runtime, so it is not possible to read an arbitrary set of priors.

It is going to be confusing to users to have gmo_glmer() in one package and have stan_glmer(*, algorithm = "gmo") in rstanarm, but if having an arbitrary set of priors is important, then I guess it will have to be that way.

Ben
